Seventeen comments

The barnacle

this goes well in a set with sonny’s mazurka,and like all mazurkas,should be played with a slighly dotted rythym.this tune is not a waltz

↳ Posted by dafydd on February 28th, 2003.

Redowa

I first heard this tune in the early 1980s. It was played, and recorded, by a band called “Iona”, who were from in and around Leeds. They called it the “Barnacle Redowa”. Checking a dictionary gave the following definition of “redowa” :
“a Bohemian folk dance similar to a waltz or a polka.”
Anyone come across the redowa before or know any others?

↳ Posted by Kenny on August 27th, 2003.

Gan Ainm by any other name - another 3-part mazurka

I was just considering this and had some vague memory of something similar already noted on site, and I was right. This 3-parter, whatever version, works out well for the Mazurka-Waltz waltzing the third part. Here’s one of several versions of it I’ve known:

Miss Lambert’s Waltz

This tune appears in the Francis Reynolds manuscript of Gaigue, Ballinamuck, Co. Longford written in the last quarter of the 19th century. The title he gives is ‘Miss Lambert’s Waltz’.

↳ Posted by ConorW on February 16th, 2015.
